title: When everything ends, the Majestic and Generous remains
subtitle: Lord of Majesty and Honour: awe and generosity in one Lord
intro: Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram (ذُوالْجَلاَلِ وَالإكْرَامِ) means the Possessor of Majesty and Honour, the One whose greatness fills the heart with awe and whose generosity fills it with hope. He alone remains when everything else passes away, so He is the one worth holding on to.

root.letters: ج ل ل / ك ر م
root.sense: Jalal is majesty and grandeur, the greatness before which one lowers the eyes, as people speak of His Majesty for a monarch. Ikram, from karam, is honour and generosity: He is the One deserving to be honoured, and the One who honours His servants with His gifts.

row.title: This world is all there is
sub: Enjoy it as if it lasts

knowing: This name gathers the two great families of His names into one phrase. {idea}Jalal is His majesty: might, greatness, the names that make you stand straight in prayer. Ikram is His generosity and honour: the names that make the heart soften.{/idea} He is both, at once and always.

Holding both together keeps the heart balanced. Too much hope without awe makes a person careless, sure that anything goes. Too much fear without hope makes a person despair, imagining a Lord who does not love. {reward}The one who knows Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram respects Him deeply and runs to Him with hope.{/reward} And the balance is not equal in weight: the Prophet ﷺ conveyed that His mercy prevails over His anger (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

Ikram also works in two directions: He is the One most worthy of being honoured, and He is the One who honours. {idea}His majesty does not make Him distant; it is the majesty of a King who seats His guests in honour.{/idea}
seeing: The phrase appears in the Quran in only two places, both in Surah Ar-Rahman. The first half of the surah is a feast of creation: sun and moon, seas, pearls, ships, the human gift of speech, each followed by the question of which favour you will deny. Then comes the turning point: everyone on earth will perish, and only the Face of your Lord remains, Lord of Majesty and Honour (55:26-27).

It is like being served every dish in a wonderful restaurant, tasting each one in delight, and then being told it closes forever tomorrow. Your heart sinks, and then lifts: if the dishes were this good, how great is the One who made them? {idea}After this verse the surah turns to the Hereafter, the life that lasts.{/idea} It closes with the second mention: blessed is the name of your Lord, Lord of Majesty and Honour (55:78).

The Prophet ﷺ made this name part of daily life. After each obligatory prayer he would say: O Allah, You are As-Salam and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Lord of Majesty and Honour (Sahih Muslim). And he told his companions to hold fast to Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram in their supplication (Jami at-Tirmidhi).
trusting: Everything you are anxious about losing will one day be gone anyway: the job, the house, the reputation, even the people you love in their earthly form. {trap}Putting your whole weight on what is passing guarantees a fall.{/trap} Put it on the One who remains.

His majesty means no situation is too big for Him; His generosity means no request is too small for Him to care about. {reward}So you can bring Him both the frightening things and the trivial ones, and leave them with a Lord who has the power and the generosity to handle them.{/reward}
loving: We are drawn to greatness and we are drawn to kindness, but rarely find both in one person. Human beings who rise in power often grow harder. {reward}In Him, majesty and generosity are perfectly joined, and the heart that sees this both bows and loves.{/reward}
now: You are clearing out a late grandparent's flat: the furniture they saved for, the clothes they loved, now in bin bags. {idea}Everything here was a gift, and everything here has passed{/idea}. Only His Face remains. Whisper Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram, and ask Him to honour them now with what lasts.
old: I put my security in things and people that I fear losing.
new: Everything passes except the Lord of Majesty and Honour, so I can enjoy His gifts while leaning on Him alone.
try: After each prayer today, say: Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram, and think about what it means.

dua.text: Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram, You alone remain when all else passes. Fill my heart with awe of Your majesty and hope in Your generosity, and honour me with nearness to You.
dua.note: The Prophet ﷺ urged holding fast to this name in dua (Jami at-Tirmidhi) and used it after every obligatory prayer (Sahih Muslim).

pairs.why: Al-Jalil is His majesty on its own; Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram joins that majesty to His honouring generosity.
Ikram comes from the same root as Al-Karim: the generosity that balances His majesty.
Only the Face of the Lord of Majesty and Honour remains when everything else perishes (55:27).

faq.a: It means the Possessor of Majesty and Honour. Jalal is His majesty and greatness, which fills the heart with awe. Ikram is His honour and generosity: He deserves to be honoured, and He honours His servants with His gifts and mercy.

faq.q: Where is Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: It appears twice, both in Surah Ar-Rahman: in 55:27, after stating that everything on earth perishes and only the Face of your Lord remains, and in 55:78, the final verse of the surah.

faq.q: When do Muslims say Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram?
faq.a: The Prophet ﷺ would say after each obligatory prayer: Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram (Sahih Muslim). He also told his companions to hold fast to calling on Allah by this name in dua (Jami at-Tirmidhi).
